epithet: The surah that pleads for its companion
lede: Thirty ayat that the Prophet ﷺ would not sleep without reciting. They open on the One in whose hand is all dominion, send the eye up to search the sky for a single flaw — and end by asking who would bring you water if yours sank away.

names.name: al-Mulk
names.note: After its first ayah: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.

names.name: Tabārak
names.note: Its first word, and the name the Prophet ﷺ used for it: “It is the surah Tabāraka lladhī bi-yadihi l-mulk” (al-Tirmidhī 2891).

names.name: al-Māniʿah
names.note: The name Ibn Masʿūd gives it: “It is the preventer from the punishment of the grave.” Al-Qurṭubī also records al-Wāqiyah, the Protector, and al-Munjiyah, the Rescuer.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all, as al-Qurṭubī puts it, and Ibn al-Jawzī records the agreement. The traditional order places it seventy-seventh. It opens the twenty-ninth juzʾ of the muṣḥaf, every surah of which is Makkan but for the dispute over al-Insān.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ المُلْكِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ قالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: هي المانِعَةُ مِن عَذابِ القَبْرِ
سُورَةُ الْمُلْكِ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ. وَتُسَمَّى الْوَاقِيَةُ وَالْمُنْجِيَةُ. وَهِيَ ثَلَاثُونَ آيَةً

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ بِمَكَّةَ سُورَةُ «تَبارَكَ» المُلْكِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: No particular occasion is reported for it. It comes from the later Makkan years, when the argument had been made many times and the surahs take on a tone of final summons: look, think, and answer.

Its hearers did not deny that Allah made the heavens. What they denied was that it placed them under any obligation, or that they would be raised to account for it. So the surah begins with why life and death exist at all — “to test you, which of you is best in deed” — and then issues a challenge unlike any other in the Qurʾan. Look at the creation of the Most Merciful: do you see any fault? Look again. Then look again, twice over — your sight will come back to you humbled and worn out.

After that it lets them hear their own future. The keepers of Hell ask each crowd thrown into it: did no warner come to you? And they answer: yes, one came, and we denied him. “Had we but listened, or used our reason, we would not be among the people of the Blaze.”

The second half is a series of questions, each beginning “Who?” or “Do you feel secure?” — who is this army of yours that will help you against the Most Merciful; who will provide for you if He withholds His provision; do you feel safe that He who is in the heaven will not make the earth swallow you. They did not have answers, and the surah does not wait for them.
aim: To display the perfection of Allah’s dominion and power — moving the hearer to awe of Him, and warning of His punishment.
themes: Life and death as a test
The regret of the people of the Fire

outline.title: The Sovereign, and His work
outline.summary: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He has power over all things: who created death and life to test which of you is best in deed; who created seven heavens in layers. You see no disproportion in the creation of the Most Merciful. Look again — do you see any rift? And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps.

outline.title: “Had we but listened”
outline.summary: For those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell. When they are flung into it they hear it draw breath as it boils, almost bursting with rage. Each time a crowd is thrown in, its keepers ask, “Did no warner come to you?” They will say, “Yes — and we denied.” And they will confess their sin.

outline.title: Those who fear Him unseen
outline.summary: Those who fear their Lord without seeing Him will have forgiveness and a great reward. Speak in secret or aloud — He knows what is in the breasts. Does He who created not know, when He is the Subtle, the Aware?

outline.title: Do you feel secure?
outline.summary: It is He who made the earth manageable for you, so walk its slopes and eat of His provision; to Him is the resurrection. Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, or send against you a storm of stones? Those before them denied — and how was My reproach?

outline.title: Who, besides the Most Merciful?
outline.summary: Do they not see the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up but the Most Merciful. Who is it that could be an army for you against Him? Who would provide for you if He withheld? Is one who walks fallen on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path? It is He who produced you and gave you hearing, sight and hearts — little thanks you give.

outline.title: When it comes
outline.summary: They say, “When is this promise?” Say: the knowledge is with Allah; I am only a clear warner. When they see it near, the faces of the disbelievers will fall. Say: He is the Most Merciful; we believe in Him, and upon Him we rely. Say: have you considered — if your water were to sink into the earth, who then could bring you flowing water?

keyAyah.why: The reason for everything: death and life were created as a test — and the test is not who does most, but who does best.

virtues.text: “There is a surah of the Qurʾan, thirty ayat, which interceded for a man until he was forgiven. It is ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion’.”
virtues.arabic: إِنَّ سُورَةً مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ثَلاَثُونَ آيَةً شَفَعَتْ لِرَجُلٍ حَتَّى غُفِرَ لَهُ

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited “Alif Lām Mīm, the sending down” — al-Sajdah — and “Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.”

“Whoever recites ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion’ every night, Allah will protect him by it from the punishment of the grave. In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to call it the Preventer.”
virtues.grade: Ḥasan according to al-Albānī (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Targhīb); a saying of Ibn Masʿūd
virtues.caveat: This is al-Albānī’s grading as an index of his works records it; it has not yet been checked here against the printed book. Two numbers are given for it in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Targhīb, so none is printed.

before: Al-Taḥrīm ended with four women — two who were lost though married to prophets, and two who were saved. Al-Mulk opens with the rule behind it: He created death and life to test which of you is best in deed.
after: Al-Mulk ends by telling the Prophet ﷺ what to say. Al-Qalam begins by telling him what he is: by the grace of your Lord you are not mad, and you are of a tremendous character.

notable.label: In whose hand is the dominion; life and death as a test

sources: The Sunan of al-Tirmidhī, Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī
